subject: More questions about control and mimic arguments in lavaan

messages.author: 93fdeb4704061276
messages.subject: More questions about control and mimic arguments in lavaan
parts:
Hello,

Yesterday I posted about "how do we get more iterations."  I'm still hoping to understand that, but overnight I've been reading more in the lavaan documentation and I've got a more general followup. I have the example code and data for your inspection.

The students suggested playing around with more settings, and I find that mimic="MPlus" or "EQS" gives a convergent result.  Now, does that mean that MPlus imitation gives a wrongly convergent result, or does lavaan's method give me a right "there's no answer".

I uploaded the data and the working test case. This is a teaching example that we use, students are encouraged to throw parameters in and out to see what happens.

You can find the material here:

http://pj.freefaculty.org/scraps/lavaan-20130501

I hope you see the files with the data, the R commands I've tried, and the output.

example-4-30-2013.R   
example-4-30-2013.Rout  
example.dat

I'm not an SEM user, just doing tech support, so take this as a minimally informed critique: It seems to me the lavaan help page needs clarification on how to change the optimizer, because, as you see in my example output file, changes that seem to be reasonable are causing a failure.  From ?lavaan, it seems as though I should be able to try BGFS:

> fit1 <- lavaan(model = mod1, data = dat, meanstructure = TRUE, control =
+                list(optim.method = "BGFS", eval.max = 40000, iter.max = 200000))
Error: OPTIMIZER %in% c("NLMINB.CONSTR", "ALABAMA") is not TRUE

With the many different parameters that need to be set, and all interacted to the mimic argument, it seems to me there are lots of dragons.  Wouldn't it be nicer to group together all of these settings in a list?

Paul Johnson
Center for Research Methods and Data Analysis
University of Kansas

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: More questions about control and mimic arguments in lavaan
parts:
Hi PJ,

I think the issue might be in the starting values that are being used. The model you posted is pretty sensitive to start values and using mimic = "Mplus" or "EQS" provide different starting values than mimic = "lavaan" Take a look at the help page for the lavaan function for more details. Also, you can access starting values using inspect(fit, "start") for any fitted lavaan object. If you try that with the models in your example, fit1 has different starting values than fit1mps and fit1eqs.

Alex

On 05/01/2013 09:31 PM, Paul Johnson wrote:
> The students suggested playing around with more settings, and I find
> that mimic="MPlus" or "EQS" gives a convergent result. Now, does that
> mean that MPlus imitation gives a wrongly convergent result, or does
> lavaan's method give me a right "there's no answer".

I don't know. I will need to study your example in more depth to
understand why the mimic= options have an influence on the
(non)-convergence. It may be the starting values, but that 'should' not
have an effect. In the ideal world.

> I'm not an SEM user, just doing tech support, so take this as a
> minimally informed critique: It seems to me the lavaan help page needs
> clarification on how to change the optimizer, because, as you see in my
> example output file, changes that seem to be reasonable are causing a
> failure. From ?lavaan, it seems as though I should be able to try BGFS:
>
>> fit1 <- lavaan(model = mod1, data = dat, meanstructure = TRUE, control =
> + list(optim.method = "BGFS", eval.max = 40000, iter.max = 200000))
> Error: OPTIMIZER %in% c("NLMINB.CONSTR", "ALABAMA") is not TRUE

Good point. The reason why optim.method = "BGFS" fails is this:

L1 == 3 - L2 - L3
L4 == 3 - L5 - L6

Constraints. The BGFS (from optim), and nlminb() optimizers are for
unconstrained problems only. Once you add explicit constraints, lavaan
switches to another optimization method, ie nlminb.constr(), which is a
custom method that I wrote.

Instead of an error message, lavaan should check for constraints, and
the content of the control() argument. Another thing I did not
anticipate ;-)

The current version of lavaan uses a brute-force method to deal with
constraints. It makes no distinction between highly complex nonlinear
constraints, and simple linear constraints. This will change in the
(hopefully near) future. The point is that we do not really need
constrained optimization techniques if the constraints are linear.

For your example, the constrained optimizers ends with the message:

convergence status (0=ok): 11
nlminb.constr message says: Convergence due to lack of progress in
parameter updates

Perhaps lavaan is too strict here, and treat this as 'converged' anyway?

Yves.
